subject.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings

question: After rebasing onto current main, should the Codex computer watchdog accept only finite numeric JSON durations, or intentionally preserve decimal-integer duration strings as a compatibility contract?
rationale: The upstream protocol transports free-form JSON but does not define this field's grammar, while the PR deliberately preserves one subset of malformed-type inputs; selecting that permanent compatibility boundary requires owner intent.

options.title: Use the numeric schema
options.body: Accept finite non-negative JSON numbers only and align watchdog budgeting with the computer tool's canonical typed argument contract.

options.title: Preserve decimal strings
options.body: Retain digit-only strings, but document the compatibility contract and prove that execution and watchdog parsing accept the same domain.

recommendation.title: Use the numeric schema
recommendation.body: Accept finite non-negative JSON numbers only and align watchdog budgeting with the computer tool's canonical typed argument contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related dynamic-tool timeout history makes them the strongest available routing candidate for the timeout-contract choice.
